correctness.rationale: For every q in (0,1), the Jacobi squared modulus has exact q^2-scaled tail, forcing descending normalized eigenvalues. Every principal determinant factors into geometric weights and consecutive Toeplitz determinants sum_{h=0}^ell a^{2h}. Partition-run displacement bounds the trace of the nth exterior power by O(q^{n(n-1)}) offcritical and q^{n(n-1)}exp(O(log^2 n)) at criticality. The leading compression supplies the matching exponential lower bounds; Cesaro monotonicity yields the exact limit. The offcritical exterior-product bound proves summable normalized excess, whereas critical leading determinants grow by n+1, proving nonsummability. Inner Blaschke factorization handles a>1; residue-chain ordering extends to fixed m. Standalone exact checker passed 852 rational identities; finite tests are supplemental, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The problem targets the precise approximation-number tail of a concrete compact Hardy weighted-composition operator whose full moment hierarchy was previously known only implicitly. The exact coefficient equals a weight Mahler measure and undergoes a structural change when the polynomial zero crosses the unit circle; a sharp summability boundary distinguishes genuine trace-like tail corrections from critical persistent spectral excess. Fixed-tap spectral ordering is useful for approximation rank and spectral truncation, and the result requires a nontrivial positive-Jacobi determinant argument beyond routine singular-value bounds.
